ClientBlockIn.description:
API 0.5 form: the tag was already programmed offline (ADR-0014).

`client_id` and `tag_token` are **both** required here. That is what makes the
two forms a closed choice rather than one model with optional halves: half an
identity can neither replay nor conflict, and a generator should refuse it
before a server has to.

client_id.description: **Your identifier for this block, unique within your tenant.** Minted before the tag is programmed and always supplied, so a registration replayed after any offline period cannot duplicate. It is **not** the canonical id: Service generates that and returns both. Two tenants may use the same value for unrelated blocks, and neither can learn anything about the other.
client_id.title: Client Id

label.description: Non-blank, up to 200 characters — the length Android's local model already accepts. Whitespace alone is not a label. The 0.4 server-minted form keeps its 120-character limit.
label.title: Label

tag_token.description: The canonical ADR-0014 token: 32 random bytes as exactly 43 characters of unpadded base64url. Send the token only — never the whole `blocks://tag/v1/<token>` URI. A padded or standard-alphabet spelling of the same bytes is refused, because two spellings would hash differently and one physical tag would become two blocks. Service stores only the hash and **never returns this value**: you already hold it.
tag_token.title: Tag Token

ClientBlockIn.title: ClientBlockIn

ClientRegisteredBlockOut.description:
Result of the API 0.5 client-supplied form.

**No `tag_token`, by construction.** You supplied it, so returning it would add
nothing — and it would not merely be displayed: idempotency persists a
response as JSON, so echoing the token would write the raw value into Service
storage, which is exactly what hashing it was for. `client_id` and the
canonical `id` are what a client needs to attribute the acknowledgement and
rewrite its dependent binding.
ClientRegisteredBlockOut.title: ClientRegisteredBlockOut

operation_id.description: **The durable identity of this mutation.** Service records a receipt bound to the complete envelope — project, item, mutation type, If-Match and payload. Resending the exact envelope acknowledges this same operation again over the item's current state, with no second write and no second event; reusing the id with any other envelope is `409`. Never rotate it on timeout, restart or an ambiguous response.
operation_id.title: Operation Id

code.description: Stable machine-readable code. Branch on this.

message.description: Human-readable prose. May change in a PATCH; do not branch on it.

EventEnvelopeOut.description:
The accepted 0.1 envelope, typed.

Published as fields rather than a bare object so a generated client gets the
stable parts — everything a consumer routes and deduplicates on. `payload`
stays open on purpose: its shape is chosen by `eventType` + `eventVersion`
and is versioned separately in the event schemas, so freezing it here would
make every new event type a breaking change to this response.

eventVersion.description: MAJOR.MINOR of the payload schema, as written.

payload.description: Identifiers and the minimum needed to act. Shape is given by `eventType` and `eventVersion`; tolerate unknown fields.
